series: trendwatching.com annual consumer trends (free Trend Briefing)
title: 12 CRUCIAL CONSUMER TRENDS FOR 2012
notes: First archived 2011-12-03. The intro calls them '12 must-know consumer trends (in random order)', so rank is print order, not priority. Labels from the numbered heading images' alt text; item 13 'MORE-ISM' is a Premium promotion, not a trend. target_year 2012 from the title. The 100+ page 2012 Trend Report (Premium) is not captured.

entries.label: RED CARPET
entries.quote: In 2012, department stores, airlines, hotels, theme parks, museums, if not entire cities and nations around the world will roll out the red carpet for the new emperors, showering Chinese visitors and customers with tailored services and perks, and in general, lavish attention and respect.
entries.subject: Services tailored to Chinese travellers and shoppers

entries.label: DIY HEALTH
entries.quote: Expect to see consumers take advantage of new technologies and apps to discreetly and continuously track, manage and be alerted to, any changes in their personal health.
entries.subject: Self-tracking of personal health

entries.label: DEALER-CHIC
entries.quote: In 2012, not only will consumers continue to hunt for deals and discounts, but they will do so with relish if not pride.
entries.subject: Deal hunting as status

entries.label: ECO-CYCOLOGY
entries.quote: Brands will increasingly take back all of their products for recycling (sometimes forced by new legislation), and recycle them responsibly and innovatively.
entries.subject: Brand take-back and recycling

entries.label: CASH-LESS
entries.quote: But a cashless future is (finally) upon us, as major players such as MasterCard and Google work to build a whole new eco-system of payments, rewards and offers around new mobile technologies.
entries.subject: Mobile and cashless payments
entries.note: Preceded by 'Will coins and notes completely disappear in 2012? No.'

entries.label: BOTTOM OF THE URBAN PYRAMID
entries.quote: the global opportunities for brands which cater to the hundreds of millions of lower-income CITYSUMERS are unprecedented.
entries.subject: Lower-income urban consumers in emerging markets
entries.note: Label printed two ways on the page: 'BOTTOM OF THE URBAN PYRAMID' (section heading, used here) and 'URBAN BOTTOM OF THE PYRAMID' (overview); abbreviated BOUP.

entries.label: IDLE SOURCING
entries.quote: Anything that makes it downright simple- if not completely effortless- for consumers to contribute to something will be more popular than ever in 2012.
entries.subject: Passive, sensor-based crowdsourcing

entries.label: FLAWSOME
entries.quote: Why to consumers, brands that behave more humanly, including exposing their flaws, will be awesome.
entries.subject: Brands showing human flaws
entries.note: The sentence reads oddly in the source ('Why to consumers'); kept verbatim.

entries.label: SCREEN CULTURE
entries.quote: Thanks to the continued explosion of touchscreen smartphones, tablets, and the 'cloud', 2012 will see a SCREEN CULTURE that is not only more pervasive, but more personal, more immersive and more interactive than ever.
entries.subject: Touchscreens and personal screens

entries.label: RECOMMERCE
entries.quote: In 2012, ‘trading in’ is the new buying.
entries.subject: Resale and trade-in of past purchases

entries.label: EMERGING MATURIALISM
entries.quote: Expect frank, risqué or non-corporate products, services and campaigns from emerging markets to be on the rise in 2012.
entries.subject: Risqué, non-corporate brands in emerging markets

entries.label: POINT & KNOW
entries.quote: 2012 will see instant visual information gratification brought into the real and visual world with objects and even people.
entries.subject: Visual search and object recognition (point a phone, get information)
